raw_case_text:
A 28-year-old male patient with a history of HIV/AIDS complicated by numerous prior opportunistic infections, presented with progressive dyspnea on exertion and chronic, nonproductive cough. He also endorsed night sweats, chills, and nonbloody diarrhea, as well as weight loss over a period of a few months. He had been off antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past 2 years. He had a history of intravenous drug use and resided at a rehabilitation facility.
On presentation, he was afebrile with unremarkable vital signs and normal oxygen saturation on room air. Physical examination was only notable for oral thrush, shotty right anterior cervical and submandibular lymphadenopathy, and faint inspiratory crackles on chest auscultation. No abnormal lesions were noted on a thorough skin examination.
Laboratory analysis was notable for a white blood count of 3 x 103/mm3and hemoglobin of 9.6 g/dL. CD4 count was 3 cells/mm3and viral load was 2,990,000 copies/mL. Renal, hepatic, and thyroid function, as well as electrolytes, were all within normal limits.
Initial chest radiograph was unremarkable. Computerized tomography (CT) of the chest showed multiple bilateral, right greater than left-sided, ill-defined peribronchovascular ground-glass nodules [Figure 1]. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast showed periportal, celiac, mesenteric, and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, as well as several low-density lesions in the liver.
An extensive infectious investigation, including blood, sputum, and fungal cultures, and viral and fungal serologies, was negative. Initial bronchoscopy was remarkable for the absence of oral, laryngeal or endobronchial lesions, and bronchoalveolar lavage was negative. Bone marrow biopsy showed myeloid maturation arrest consistent with AIDS with no evidence of lymphoma or KS.
Sequential thallium 201 and gallium 67 scintigraphy was notable for abnormal delayed thallium uptake in and the absence of gallium uptake, raising concern for pulmonary KS over lymphoproliferative disorders or opportunistic infections [Figure 2]. Based on these findings, the patient underwent an ultrasound-guided core biopsy of a sub-centimeter submandibular lymph node which revealed central sarcomatoid proliferation with positive immunohistochemical staining for CD31, CD34, and HHV-8, confirming the diagnosis of KS [Figure 3].
Treatment with doxorubicin was initiated, and ART was resumed. On completion of two cycles of chemotherapy, the patient developed worsening pancytopenia and neutropenic fever. Repeat thoracic imaging was notable for significant progression of the ill-defined peribronchovascular infiltrates, interlobular septal thickening, and mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy [Figure 4]. The patient's course was complicated by bland alveolar hemorrhage due to progressive pulmonary KS and severe thrombocytopenia. Repeat bronchoscopy revealed characteristic red to slightly violaceous macular lesions in the endobronchial tree, not seen on examination 2 months prior [Figure 5]. The patient was deemed too ill to tolerate further chemotherapy or radiation for treatment of KS. His symptoms worsened, and he expired shortly thereafter.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 28-year-old male with advanced untreated HIV/AIDS presented with a several-month history of progressive exertional dyspnea, chronic nonproductive cough, night sweats, chills, non-bloody diarrhea, and weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Having discontinued antiretroviral therapy 2 years earlier, the patient experienced progressively worsening shortness of breath on exertion and a chronic dry cough over several months, accompanied by drenching night sweats, chills, watery non-bloody diarrhea, and unintentional weight loss.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of HIV/AIDS complicated by multiple prior opportunistic infections; off antiretroviral therapy for the past 2 years; history of intravenous drug use, currently residing at an inpatient rehabilitation facility.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for progressive exertional dyspnea, dry cough, night sweats, chills, non-bloody diarrhea, weight loss, and oral thrush; negative for cutaneous lesions.

objective.physical_examination: On admission, afebrile with normal vital signs and normal room-air oxygen saturation. Physical examination revealed oropharyngeal candidiasis (thrush), shotty right anterior cervical and submandibular lymphadenopathy, faint bilateral inspiratory pulmonary crackles, and a completely normal skin examination without mucocutaneous Kaposi sarcoma lesions.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs showed leukopenia (WBC 3.0 x 10^3/mm3) and anemia (hemoglobin 9.6 g/dL), with normal renal, hepatic, and thyroid function and normal electrolytes. Blood, sputum, and fungal cultures as well as viral and fungal serologies were negative. Initial chest radiograph was unremarkable.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission CD4+ T-cell count was 3 cells/mm3. Chest CT demonstrated bilateral (right greater than left) ill-defined peribronchovascular ground-glass nodules; contrast-enhanced abdomen/pelvis CT showed periportal, celiac, mesenteric, and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy and multiple hypodense hepatic lesions. Initial bronchoscopy and BAL were negative for endobronchial lesions or pathogens, and bone marrow biopsy showed AIDS-related myeloid maturation arrest without lymphoma or KS. Sequential Thallium-201 and Gallium-67 scintigraphy revealed delayed thallium-avid, gallium-negative pulmonary uptake characteristic of Kaposi sarcoma, and ultrasound-guided core biopsy of a sub-centimeter submandibular lymph node confirmed Kaposi sarcoma (central sarcomatoid spindle-cell proliferation positive for CD31, CD34, and HHV-8). Repeat chest CT and bronchoscopy 2 months later (after 2 cycles of doxorubicin and ART resumption) demonstrated marked progression of peribronchovascular infiltrates, interlobular septal thickening, hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy, bland alveolar hemorrhage, and new red-to-violaceous endobronchial macular KS lesions.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Visceral/nodal and bronchopulmonary Kaposi sarcoma presenting without cutaneous involvement in a 28-year-old male with advanced AIDS (CD4+ count 3 cells/mm3, plasma HIV viral load 2,990,000 copies/mL), confirmed by thallium-positive/gallium-negative lung scintigraphy, CD31+/CD34+/HHV-8+ submandibular lymph node core biopsy, and subsequent endobronchial violaceous macules on repeat bronchoscopy. Despite resumption of ART and two cycles of systemic doxorubicin chemotherapy, the patient developed worsening pancytopenia, neutropenic fever, severe thrombocytopenia, progressive pulmonary KS (possibly exacerbated by KS-IRIS), and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, and died shortly thereafter.
